slides.title: Model Risk Factory
slides.lead: Evidence and human review throughout the model lifecycle
points: Legacy SAS / R code becomes documented Python scoring code with a tested reference.
Documentation approval and validation sign-off remain human decisions.
slides.notes: Introduce the model-risk workflow. This is a prototype with offline verification, not a claim of production or regulatory approval.

slides.title: The operational problem
slides.lead: Legacy models spread evidence across code, spreadsheets and review documents
points: Reviewers need to connect each claim and number to its source.
Code migration needs record-level agreement with an independently supplied reference.
Monitoring findings must return to an accountable reviewer.
slides.notes: Explain the user problem without assigning an invented manual cost or completion time.

slides.title: The model lifecycle
slides.lead: One workflow connects documentation, migration and monitoring
table: Python code, parity certificate, validation report
Quality checks, drift alerts, periodic reports
slides.notes: Show the Review queue. Explain that exhausted retries or low confidence lead to manual review.

slides.title: Application architecture
slides.lead: A single API process coordinates agents, tools and persistent evidence
points: Streamlit and REST clients submit asynchronous jobs to the LangGraph workflow.
MCP tools parse code, retrieve knowledge, profile data, score candidates and compute metrics.
SQLite / Cosmos store records. Azure Files or managed-identity Blob storage hold artefacts.
Azure Container Apps runs one API replica, with a scheduled monitoring trigger.
slides.notes: The separate architecture PDF shows the component relationships. The job queue is in-process, so horizontal API scaling needs a different queue architecture.

slides.title: Python rebuild and parity
slides.lead: Each candidate must match supplied reference scores before certification
points: The agent attempts LLM translation and can fall back to transcription of exported regression parameters.
A restricted scoring subprocess compares each reference record using the configured tolerance.
Mismatch feedback returns to the next attempt. The certificate identifies the code hash.
Current SAS/R fixture scores use Python reproduction. Independent legacy-runtime exports remain pending.
slides.notes: Show the new Start Python rebuild control, generated score function and certificate. Do not describe Python-reproduced reference scores as independently executed SAS/R.

slides.title: Validation evidence
slides.lead: Stored tool results supply every reported number
table: Record-level parity against supplied reference scores
AUC, Gini, KS, Brier and calibration where applicable
Score PSI and feature distribution checks
Segment approval rates, impact ratios and error rates
slides.notes: Metrics depend on dataset roles and available targets. Missing evidence is unassessed. Documentation-only Python models do not receive a parity certificate.

slides.title: Monitoring and revalidation
slides.lead: A failed batch produces a visible finding and an accountable next step
points: Quality failures reject the batch before model scoring.
Amber and red drift generate alerts. Red drift returns the workflow to validation and a new H2 review.
Scheduled reports preserve batch metrics and their sources.
The demo's drift batches are synthetic and must be described as such.
slides.notes: Show a rejected batch and its reason, then a drift alert. Thresholds are team policy rather than a regulatory certification.

slides.title: Business case measurement
slides.lead: Savings need a measured manual baseline and deployment evidence
points: Record manual documentation and migration effort separately from human approval waiting time.
Measure agent processing time, retries and tokens on the intended real LLM configuration.
Compute portfolio scenarios from measured per-model inputs and label them as projections.
No measured manual baseline is available, so this deck makes no savings or ROI claim.
slides.notes: Use the baseline worksheet. Offline mock latency and mock token estimates are not production cost evidence.

slides.title: Responsible AI and review boundaries
slides.lead: The system assists reviewers and preserves evidence for their decisions
points: Input guards screen common personal-data and prompt-injection patterns, with known blind spots.
The document rater checks citations and vetoes invented variables or unsupported numbers.
H1 and H2 record a human actor. Evaluation auto-approvals are labelled simulation events.
Real LLM calibration, fairness interpretation and policy approval require owner sign-off.
slides.notes: The knowledge base is a team paraphrase. The official SS1/23 index now lists the April 2026 revision. This prototype does not establish regulatory compliance.
